To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

caveolin- 1 functions as a tumor suppressor in mammary epithelium and as a tumor promoter (oncogene) in prostatic epithelium, and that the molecular mechanisms underlying these opposing activities are related to phosphorylation and mutation of caveolin-1.
caveolin- 1 functions as a tumor and/or metastasis suppressor in breast and ovarian cancers, and as a tumor and metastasis promoter in prostate cancers.

caveolin-1, a tumor and/or metastasis suppressor gene, functions as a negative growth regulator of normal mammary epithelial cells; caveolin-1 mutations (P132 L) and phosphorylation (Tyr14 and Ser80), however, may override or inactiviate the growth inhibitory activities of the caveolin scaffolding domain (residue 82-101), and thereby function as oncogenes in human prostate and breast cancer cells, respectively.

the molecular mechanisms by which caveolin-1 regulates oncogenesis and metastasis.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

caveolin- 1 is a tumor modifier gene that can either promote or suppress tumor progression depending on the cellular context and the specific molecular events occurring within the tumor microenvironment.
Cav-1 is a "tumor modifier gene" that can function either as a tumor suppressor gene or a tumor promoter gene.
caveolin-2 is a "dual function tumor modifier gene" whose role is dependent on the cellular context and the nature of the cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

caveolin- 1 may function as both a tumor suppressor and a tumor promoter, depending on its subcellular localization (i.e., membrane vs. cytosol) and/or its post-translational modification (phosphorylation vs. acylation).

caveolin- 1 is a multifunctional protein that may act as a tumor and/or metastasis suppressor gene, a tumor and/or progression promoter gene, or both, depending on the cellular context and/or the specific molecular mechanism involved in the oncogenic process.
caveolin- 1 functions as a tumor and/or metastasis suppressor gene in breast cancer and prostate cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
caveolin- 1 is a "tumor modifier" whose activity is regulated by phosphorylation and/or mutation.
caveolin- 1 can function as a tumor and/or metastasis promoter and suppressor depending on the cellular environment, the cell type, and the stage of tumorigenesis.
Cav-1 functions as a "gatekeeper" in the pathogenesis and/or progression of human cancers.
